solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nuns on ridge in vocal group

parts.note: nuns are sisters of a religious order
a ledge is a narrow ridge or shelf of rock

explanation.surface: Nuns perched on a mountain ridge singing together in a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuns' tempts towards a convent choir as the definition; the vocal group is a family pop act, and the nuns only supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister Sledge were an American family band of singing sisters, famous for disco hits.

clue.text: Spindle wounded daughter, cracking

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged and knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter pricked by a spindle, as in Sleeping Beauty, suffering a nasty injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like part of the injury story but is the definition in its informal British sense of excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking is British informal praise meaning first-rate, a close synonym of splendid.

clue.text: Publicly announce metal group's break- up?

indicators.note: a group's break-up scatters its members, so the letters of the phrase are split and rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band announcing its split to fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'break-up' is not a band splitting but the letters of METAL GROUP being reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To promulgate a law or decree is to make it known officially to the public.

clue.text: Herb swallowed at last by crook

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word swallowed

parts.note: its last letter is D
crook is Australian and British slang for ill or unwell

explanation.surface: A herb eaten by a criminal at the end of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but is the informal adjective for sick; 'by' simply puts ILL next to D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery aromatic plant used to flavour fish and pickles.

clue.text: Enlightened and elevated, I beat two crossing Scots isle

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means raised up, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: the two Is cross, that is go either side of, the isle

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of spiritual enlightenment after beating two others on a trip across a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Build I + TAN + I MULL I, giving ITANIMULLI, then 'elevated' turns it upward. The definition is a noun use: the Illuminati are the enlightened ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The Illuminati were a secret society claiming special knowledge; the name literally means those who are enlightened.

clue.text: So tense, American seen outside hospital

indicators.note: the outer letters are placed around the hospital letter, being outside it

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
US stands for American, as in US forces
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A nervous American spotted waiting outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective about the American's mood; it is the grammatical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so both mean therefore, or in this manner.

clue.text: Small girl heading north finds badger

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Sarah is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A little girl travelling north discovers a badger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal she finds; it is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, the same as harass.

clue.text: Goodness! Saint with sloshed laic becomes obscure

parts.note: My! is an exclamation of surprise like Goodness!

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, so the letters of laic stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Shock as a saint and a drunken layman together turn incomprehensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laic' means a layperson, not clergy; its letters become ICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mystical has a hidden spiritual meaning, so it is obscure or beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Just one Roman poet's written about power

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters are written around the power letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Martial was a Latin poet famous for his epigrams
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Just one Roman poet has written about power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only' but is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just judge is fair and even-handed, treating all sides equally without bias.

clue.text: Overweight villain in film

definitions.meaning: first meaning: weighing a lot, fat
second meaning: in film and theatre the ... is the bad guy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fat movie villain, but the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy describes great weight, and as a noun it is the actor cast as the menacing antagonist.

clue.text: Short account about Channel Island current

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the island
short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tale is an account of events
Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.surface: A brief account of the sea currents around a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a sea current but is a rising air current. HERM is a small island between Guernsey and Sark.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a column of rising warm air, used by gliders and soaring birds.

clue.text: Disliked newcomer stumped in superior role

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior

indicators.note: the stumped letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A resented arrival, baffled by being given a senior job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped' looks like baffled; in cricket a batsman is stumped when the wicket-keeper breaks the wicket, written ST.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves arrogantly, and is resented for it.

clue.text: Neverending journey made free

indicators.note: never ending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: An endless journey finally liberated someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rid is the past tense of rid, to free or clear something of an unwanted thing.

clue.text: Columnist is for slamming 1/24 hit

indicators.note: slamming means knocking hard, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist criticising a Sister Sledge hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slamming' looks like a critic attacking; it signals rearranging COLUMNIST IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost in Music was a 1979 disco single by Sister Sledge, written by Chic's Rodgers and Edwards.

clue.text: Cave deposit no longer fresh — work with it inside

indicators.note: the work and it pieces go inside the stale word

parts.note: stale food is no longer fresh
to act is to work or operate

explanation.surface: A stale cave formation, with someone told to work it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is a mineral icicle hanging from a cave roof, formed by dripping water.

clue.text: One revelling in somewhat tight score, needing runs

parts.note: merry is British slang for slightly drunk, short of fully tight
to make a run or goal is to score it
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer celebrating in a close game, needing more runs to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight score' looks like a close match; 'tight' means drunk and 'score' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A merrymaker is a person joining in festivities, celebrating with drink and fun.

clue.text: Ancient region lately evacuated, charity recalled

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outer letters of lately remain
recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: aid is charity, help given to those in need

explanation.surface: A region evacuated recently, with charity workers called home.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia was a kingdom of western Asia Minor, ruled by Croesus, in present-day Turkey.

clue.text: Wiseacre in LA beginning to talk in vulgar language

indicators.note: the wiseacre word is put inside LA

parts.note: an owl is a byword for a wise one, and wiseacre means a know-all

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of talk

explanation.surface: A know-it-all in Los Angeles starting to speak in coarse language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vulgar' suggests rude talk; here it means of the common people, as in the Vulgate.
explanation.definitionFit: Low Latin is the popular, non-classical Latin of the later Roman period and Middle Ages.

clue.text: Ottoman officer edges away from infidel

indicators.note: the edges, that is the first and last letters, are taken away

parts.note: a pagan is an unbeliever, an infidel

explanation.surface: A Turkish officer edging away from an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges away' sounds like moving off; here it removes the edge letters of PAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga was a title for a military commander or official in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Impressive flower by river in country

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ural is a major river of Russia

explanation.surface: A striking bloom growing beside a river out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword trick for something that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things situated in the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: Response from sappers joining battle

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British army's sappers
action is fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: Military engineers answer by joining the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is the response something provokes, an answering action or feeling.

clue.text: Wife early, dancing round before noon for 1/24 hit

indicators.note: dancing round means whirling about, so all these letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A wife up early, dancing around the house in the morning to a Sister Sledge hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix WIFE EARLY together with AM to spell the song title.
explanation.definitionFit: We Are Family was Sister Sledge's best-known 1979 disco single, an anthem of togetherness.

clue.text: Animal in mountain pasture a feline lacking tail

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain pasture in Switzerland

indicators.note: lacking tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: An animal in a high meadow: a cat with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated South American camelid, bred for its soft wool.

clue.text: Fool starts with absolutely stupid statement

indicators.note: starts means taking the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A fool begins with an utterly stupid remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a silly person, from the donkey's reputation for stupidity.

clue.text: See 1
A special check for bituminous substance

parts.note: to check something is to halt it

explanation.surface: A special inspection to test road surfacing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a black tarry mixture of bitumen and gravel used to surface roads.

clue.text: Good riddance to thin-faced kinswoman?

indicators.note: good riddance says something is got rid of, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: gaunt means haggard and thin in the face

explanation.surface: Relief at being rid of a haggard female relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good riddance' reads as a stock phrase; split it, Good is G and riddance removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a female relative, the sister of one's parent.

clue.text: Pressure to cause irritation for yak

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to rattle someone is to unsettle or irritate them

explanation.surface: Pressure put on to annoy a Tibetan ox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yak' looks like the animal; it is the slang verb for chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is to talk at length about trivial things, as prattle means.

clue.text: Sunak's written about Old English verse

indicators.note: the PM letters are written around the other pair, enclosing them

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister, PM

explanation.surface: Rishi Sunak has written something about Old English poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the British Prime Minister when this was set, hence PM.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem is a piece of verse, writing in metrical lines.

clue.text: Ancient Peruvian preserved?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the Inca people of old Peru
second meaning, split in two: food that is preserved is put in a can

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical split: IN CAN is how tinned food is preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan means of the Inca civilisation, the empire centred on Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Girl embracing boy after the 14 or 21 vis- à-vis 1/24?

indicators.note: after places the girl piece after THE
embracing means holding the boy piece inside

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A girl hugging a boy after hearing a Sister Sledge hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says either of the two song entries could serve as the band's signature tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is the tune identified with a performer, as these hits are with Sister Sledge.
